[color=#ffff00][head=3]Section 11: Escalation Guidelines[/head][/color]
[color=#a4885c]11.1[/color] Escalate conflicts reasonably. Use common sense when deciding how far a situation should go. A spilled drink might lead to an argument or fistfight, but it should not normally escalate into a gunfight. ★
[color=#a4885c]11.2[/color] Use words and intimidation before lethal force. When starting or escalating a conflict, you should talk, posture, threaten violence, brandish a weapon, or fire a warning shot before attempting to kill someone. ★
[color=#a4885c]11.2A[/color] Use non-lethal options when appropriate. Command, security, and antagonists such as pirates are expected to carry and attempt to use non-lethal options before resorting to lethal force. Other roles with access to non-lethals should also make a reasonable effort to use them first. Punching someone is considered non-lethal. ★
[color=#a4885c]11.3[/color] Accept surrender. If someone offers a genuine surrender, you must accept it, regardless of how heated the situation has become. ★
[color=#a4885c]11.4[/color] Do not fake surrender. You may not intentionally offer a false surrender. ★
[color=#a4885c]11.4A[/color] Exceptions are made for those in factions. You may fake surrender but it will have heavy IC consequences placed on each faction’s SoP. ★
[color=#a4885c]11.5[/color] Do not intentionally round-remove players. If you kill someone, you are expected to revive them when it is safe to do so. You may restrain them first. If they attempt to escape and you are forced to kill them again, you are not required to revive them a second time, but you must preserve their body. ★
